summary: Joseph Prabhu works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, having studied under Bernard Williams, Alasdair MacIntyre, and doctoral supervisor John N. Findlay. He held posts at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007) and several visiting professorships.

Joseph Ratzinger (1927–2022) was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Munich (~1947–1951) and Ducal Georgianum (1949–1951). He held university posts at Munich, Bonn, Münster, Tübingen, and Regensburg between ~1958 and ~1977.

Joseph Rock (1884–1962) was a sinologist and tibetologist. He held posts at the Mid-Pacific Institute (~1908), University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1908, 1911–1920), the USDA (~1920–1924), Mills College, and the Army Map Service (1944).

Joseph Tiefenthaler (1710–1785) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. A Jesuit missionary with the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773, he also served as Rector of the Jesuit High School of Agra.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud (1795–1867) worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies after studying under Silvestre de Sacy. He held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, INALCO, and served as president of the Société Asiatique.

Linguist Joseph Vendryes (1875–1960) studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1894–1901) under Antoine Meillet (~1898–1901). He held major posts at the University of Paris (~1907–1946), École Normale Supérieure (~1920–1946), and EPHE (~1925–1946).

Joseph Walser is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenberg, and David S. Pacini. He was affiliated with Loyola University Chicago, attested in 1998.

Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall (1774–1856) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (~1789–1799). He founded Fundgruben des Orients and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1847–1849).
Josho Nozawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi. He held a professorship at Koyasan University, attested in 1950.

Joshu Sasaki (1907–2014) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Zuiryo-ji under Joten Soko Miura. He served as abbot at Yotoku-in (1948–1953), Shojuan (1953), and Mount Baldy Zen Center, which he founded, until 2012.

Joshua Ereshefsky is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. As attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of James A. Benn.

Joshua Marshman (1768–1837) worked in Indology, sinology, and linguistics. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (~1794–1799) and under Johannes Lassar (~1805–1810), and founded Serampore College in 1818.

Linguist Joshua Timothy Katz (born 1969) studied at Yale, Oxford, and Harvard. He held the Cotsen Professorship at Princeton University (1998–2022) and became a Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute around 2022.
Joshua W. C. Cutler is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Geshe Wangyal. In 2004, he was attested holding a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center.

Philosopher Josiah Royce (1855–1916) studied at the University of California, Berkeley, the University of Göttingen under Hermann Lotze, and Johns Hopkins. He taught at UC Berkeley (~1878–1882) and served on the Harvard University faculty from 1882 to 1916.

José Ignacio Cabezón (born 1956) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Caltech, UW–Madison, and Sera Monastery, later holding posts at Iliff School of Theology (~1989–2001) and UC Santa Barbara from 2001.
Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby, attested in 2012.

Jowita Kramer (born 1974) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at Hamburg (doctoral supervisor Lambert Schmithausen) and Munich, later holding posts at Munich (2017–2021) and the University of Leipzig as Professor from 2021.

Joy Brennan works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. She earned a PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, and Constance Furey, and studied under Diane Martin (attested 2015).

Joyce Burkhalter Flueckiger (born 1952) specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Goshen College (~1970–1974) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1975–1984), later holding a post at Emory University (~1992) where she became Professor Emerita.
